study_design: Retrospective known-bug test prioritization on eight predeclared bug/fix pairs; NOT blind
source: BugsInPy pinned metadata 11c5f1eea954a42132cfd06bf257766a7963e0fd; three licensed upstream repos cloned in throwaway CI
selected_test_bank: Fixed commit test module copied to both versions (post-fix, potentially regression-informed)
detection_rule: FAIL assertion on buggy with PASS on fixed for exact same collected runtime test id
scientific_conclusion: At budget 12 all three fixed policies exposed exactly 2/8 known defects, and 2/4 of the defects with a confirming assertion in this test bank. At budgets 3 and 6 lexical and one fixed-seed random ordering found 1/8 while structural diversity found 0/8. No policy is shown generally superior with n=8 and three correlated projects.
limitations: Four out of eight known defects are not detectable by ANY test of the selected corrected-revision test files according to the strict assertion PASS/FAIL primary rule; these are not environment blockers.
Many bugs rely on regression tests deliberately written knowing the fix; policy outputs do not know outcomes, but test bank is not blind.
Only three projects and eight defect pairs: defect outcomes are not statistically independent within each upstream project.
All methods use the same one-time test status observations; state and time effects are not directly estimated.

At budget 12 suites shorter than 12 tests are completely evaluated and effective budgets were clamped; results are correctly compared within each case but differing bank sizes limit cross-case inference.
The expected uniform-random counts are exact conditional expectations based on revealing tests, not a sample of 8 new defects or randomized repeated failures.
The first revealing ranks beyond budget 12 are diagnostics only and were NOT used to change predeclared budgets.
No new bug was discovered, no AI model or autonomous agent was evaluated, and no paid API was used.
next_step: Audit why four cases have no strict assertion-revealing test; distinguish oracle adequacy vs error/skip/warning and prepare a separate preregistered study of static test relevance and a genuinely new holdout cohort; do not adapt these policies on this cohort then call it validation.
